newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Manufacturers would welcome A$ rate -Costello.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Manufacturers would welcome A$ rate -Costello.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday that manufacturers would welcome recent exchange rate movements for the Australian dollar.
"What a manufacturer thought about exchange rates movements, I'd have no doubt that they would welcome it," Costello told reporters after the release of March quarter gross domestic product data.
But Costello said the government did not target a particular level for the Australian dollar.
"I never have and I never will indicate a particular level of the currency ... we have never targetted a particular level of the currency," he told reporters.

The Australian dollar has fallen to around US$0.7610 at midday on Wednesday from US$0.7770 on the morning of May 23, when the Reserve Bank took the market by surprise with a 0.5 percentage point cut in official cash rates to 5.5 percent.
Asked about the manufacturing industry's flat performance over the past two years, Costello said the higher exchange rate had been a contributing factor.
"The other, of course, was that interest rates were strong throughout 1995 and ... only started to be reduced during the course of 1996/97 (to June 30)," he said.
He said the lower dollar and the flow-on from four official interest rate cuts would help the industry pick up.
Official data released earlier on Wednesday showed GDP grew 0.9 percent in the quarter for an annual rate of 2.4 percent.
The data showed manufacturing production fell 2.2 percent, seasonally-adjusted, in the year to the March quarter.
